original_text:
Cilia and Flagella
Hair-like structures that extend from the cell surface Cilia: short, present in large numbers in certain cells
Flagella: longer and far less numerous on the particular cells in which they’re present
Membrane on the outer surface; inside, -two central tubules surrounded by nine pairs of microtubules 
Functions:
Assist in movement
Cilia in inner ear vibrate and help detect sound
Cilia present in protistsmove the cells through water like oars; sweep water and food particles into mouth-like opening
Flagella used to propel cells like protistsand sperm
explanation: Cilia and flagella are hair-like organelles that extend outward from the cell surface. Cilia are relatively short and typically present in large numbers on a cell, whereas flagella are longer and much less numerous. Structurally, both are covered by an outer membrane and contain a internal core of two central microtubules surrounded by nine pairs of outer microtubules. Cilia and flagella function in cell movement or sensory roles: flagella propel cells (such as protists and sperm), while cilia can move protists through water like oars, sweep food/water particles into mouth-like openings, or vibrate in the inner ear of multicellular organisms to assist in sound detection.

questions.q: What is the structural arrangement of microtubules inside cilia and flagella?
opts: A random bundle of tubulin fibers
Two central tubules surrounded by nine pairs of microtubules
Three central tubules surrounded by nine triplets of microtubules
Nine central tubules surrounded by two pairs of microtubules
questions.exp: Inside cilia and flagella, there are two central tubules surrounded by nine pairs of microtubules.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-locomotive function of cilia mentioned on this page?
opts: Vibrating in the inner ear to help detect sound
Synthesizing proteins for the endomembrane system
Pumping calcium ions into the smooth ER
questions.exp: The slide states that cilia in the inner ear vibrate and help detect sound, which is a sensory function rather than movement of the cell itself.
